title: Personality, memory, and controlled agency
summary: A research briefing on maintaining a consistent scientific assistant while keeping process authority outside the model.
scope: 23 focused paper reviews. Findings inform proposed experiments; no local model or security boundary has been evaluated.

observations.title: Self-description can improve while behavior worsens
observations.observation: Human Simulacra: adding RAG raises GPT-4-Turbo self-report from 78.67 to 85.33, while observer score falls from 69.00 to 65.50.
observations.implication: Assess personality through decisions and responses under pressure, alongside questionnaires.
observations.caveat: Different rubrics; eleven fictional characters. These scores do not establish human personality or security behavior.

observations.title: The alignment table qualifies the headline claim
observations.observation: PAS reports questionnaire error of 8.89 for Llama-3-8B, versus 6.81 for few-shot GPT-4o. Lower is better; this comparison contradicts a blanket superiority claim.
observations.implication: Read the metric and comparison cells before treating a method as the preferred baseline.
observations.caveat: Approximately 20% of GPT-4o queries refused and were excluded. Questionnaire error is not long-term persona retention.

observations.title: Better imitation need not mean better emotional fit
observations.observation: EmoCharacter: RoleLLM increases GPT-3.5 semantic similarity from 0.208 to 0.230, but reduces emotion consistency from 0.439 to 0.399.
observations.implication: Keep professional traits stable while allowing tone to respond appropriately to context.
observations.caveat: Six fictional characters and short dialogues. Another table reports 0.397 rather than 0.399.

observations.title: Memory can improve one constraint and damage another
observations.observation: NCP-Bench: HiAgent reduces GPT-4o-mini commitment conflicts from 26% to 4%, while player-input conflicts rise from 13% to 38%.
observations.implication: Score retained commitments, responsiveness, and task completion separately after each memory change.
observations.caveat: Interactive fiction with automated players and auditors. These rates cannot be transferred to an access-control workflow.

observations.title: A deterministic compiler can preserve a wrong directive
observations.observation: Notes2Skills: replacing adjudicated extraction with model extraction reduces action accuracy from 100% to 68.2% in one session, and 77.8% to 22.2% in another.
observations.implication: Validate extracted meaning, source qualifications, and authority before converting a note into an executable step.
observations.caveat: Three sessions and 48 downstream files. Action agreement is not a measured security-violation rate.
evidence_locations: Table 13, PDF p. 16; reviewed September 2026 v2

observations.title: An open-weight backbone is not a fully local experiment
observations.observation: AMA's Qwen3-8B LoCoMo score improves from 0.696 to 0.707 over full context. The study still uses hosted embeddings and a hosted evaluator.
observations.implication: Re-evaluate the complete local pipeline, including retrieval, embeddings, judging, and runtime settings.
observations.caveat: The reported score is model-judged. Replacing supporting components may change quality, latency, and memory behavior.

observations.title: Confident judging remains fallible
observations.observation: In the evaluation-uncertainty study, GPT-4o achieves 0.684 judgment accuracy in the 0.8–1.0 confidence bin on Olympic 2024 questions.
observations.implication: Use model judgments as measured aids; verify action traces independently and calibrate subjective ratings against humans.
observations.caveat: Confidence means verdict-token probability. The table omits the bin count, limiting interpretation.

observations.title: High detection AUC can hide late or missed detection
observations.observation: MemPot's HealthMagicCare/IKEA setting reports AUROC 0.96, but true-positive rate 0.42 at 1% false-positive rate. Mean first-detection time is nine turns in this setting.
observations.implication: Measure leakage before detection, alert delay, false alarms, and benign utility at the intended operating point.
observations.caveat: Detection under the paper's threat model does not establish interception before disclosure or feasibility on local hardware.

observations.title: A reported improvement does not match its table cells
observations.observation: SpecBench reports Qwen3-14B-thinking alignment of 57.32, rising to 62.92 with Align3: 5.60 percentage points. Adjacent prose claims 6.29.
observations.implication: Preserve exact cells, versions, and calculations when comparing candidate methods.
observations.caveat: The composite metric mixes safety and behavioral preferences. It is not an unauthorized-action rate.
evidence_locations: Table 2 and adjacent prose, PDF p. 7; reviewed arXiv v3

observations.title: The long-context comparison also changes the pass rule
observations.observation: LongSafety reports Llama-3.1-8B at 74.2% on short inputs and 13.4% on long inputs. Long-input success requires passing both instruction positions; short-input success uses one condition.
observations.implication: Hold the scoring rule constant when isolating context-length effects.
observations.caveat: This asymmetry limits a simple causal interpretation of the drop. The benchmark measures content safety, not resource authorization.

observations.title: Withdrawal changes how a paper can be used
observations.observation: Logic Agent was withdrawn in December 2024 because its experiments contained errors. Its earlier reported improvements are excluded from positive evidence here.
observations.implication: Track publication status alongside the retained source, rather than relying on a downloaded PDF alone.
observations.caveat: The historical proposal remains readable. It supplies no dependable performance evidence for this design.

observations.title: Keep persona, memory, and authority separate
observations.observation: Our proposed architecture gives each a separate role: persona defines communication; memory stores revisable evidence; authoritative workflow state determines permitted actions.
observations.implication: Require typed action proposals, current preconditions, independent permission checks, and verified execution receipts.
observations.caveat: This is an engineering proposal informed by the papers. It has not been implemented or security-qualified.
evidence_locations: Design synthesis; not a paper-reported implementation result

open_questions.question: Which traits must remain stable, and which aspects of tone should adapt?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Warmth, brevity, evidence standards, and willingness to disagree need separate behavioral criteria.

open_questions.question: What evidence permits a memory update, and who can approve a change in procedure?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Useful corrections need scope and expiry. Conversation alone cannot establish a new permission.

open_questions.question: What survives when every model, embedding, and evaluator runs locally?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Published configurations often use hosted components. Hardware, latency, and model capability may alter the result.

open_questions.question: Does curated memory improve behavior enough to justify its added failure modes?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Compare a fixed prompt, reviewed examples, and small case memory before steering, fine-tuning, or adding agents.

open_questions.question: What evidence would justify advancing beyond synthetic practice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Define acceptable false denials, evidence errors, personality drift, and forbidden proposals or effects before model comparison.

design_principles.title: Specify observable behavior
design_principles.principle: Define calm disagreement, useful clarification, candid uncertainty, and accurate status reporting. Test behavior across pressure, delay, and correction.

design_principles.title: Keep action authority outside generation
design_principles.principle: The model proposes an action. Separate software checks identity, approval, scope, version, expiry, and workflow state before execution.

design_principles.title: Make memory traceable and revisable
design_principles.principle: Retain source, scope, timestamps, uncertainty, and supersession. Review promotion into durable memory; keep policy and persona changes separate.

design_principles.title: Measure independent failure dimensions
design_principles.principle: Separate personality, claim support, missing prerequisites, legitimate completion, false denial, and unauthorized effects. Preserve failures rather than averaging them away.

design_principles.title: Change one component at a time
design_principles.principle: Freeze the baseline and held-out scenarios. Compare changes under the same task and resource budget; retain versions, regression results, and rollback.
